newsitem.title: MEXICO: Army deny capture of Mexican guerrilla leader.
newsitem.headline: Army deny capture of Mexican guerrilla leader.

text.p: The Mexican army denied on Thursday it had captured a top commander of the Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR) guerrilla group.
A military source had said late on Wednesday that the army captured an EPR leader known as Commander Hermenegildo during a gunbattle on Tuesday in the southwestern state of Guerrero.
But the 9th Military Region, which has jurisdiction over the state, said in a statement the report published by Mexican media "lacked foundation and it is not known who started it."
Hermenegildo was the name used by the author of several communiques sent by the Marxist rebel group involved in at least two gunbattles with authorities since Saturday.

The 9th Region had earlier said three soldiers and two gunmen were killed in Tuesday's incident, which took place in the hot, dusty peasant town of Atoyac de Alvarez, some 40 miles (62 km) northwest of Acapulco. The gunmen, carrying AK-47 assault rifles, were later identified as EPR members.

The EPR first appeared in the state at the end of June 1996 calling for the overthrow of President Ernesto Zedillo's government. It launched a series of attacks last year but had not attacked this year until Saturday, when rebels distributing propaganda opened fire when an army patrol came upon them on a remote road about 60 miles (100 km) east of the state capital Chilpancingo.
At least two soldiers and two rebels died in that battle.
